status_summary: Executive Order 14225 (2025-03-01) directed expanded timber production and streamlined consultation and NEPA review, and Executive Order 14308 (2025-06-12) directed consolidation of federal wildland fire programs and reviews of rules that impede prevention. USDA announced a $200 million national active forest management strategy on 2025-05-29 with a goal of 25 percent more national forest harvest and 4 billion board feet annually by fiscal year 2028. In 2026 the Forest Service proposed rescinding the 2001 Roadless Rule (91 FR 53827, 2026-08-20, comments due 2026-09-21), Interior published two notices establishing BLM timber salvage and thinning categorical exclusions effective 2026-08-24, and on 2026-10-13 the Forest Service published a final rule shortening and simplifying its project objection process (91 FR 64760), effective 2026-11-12. No verified data on timber sold or harvested since 2025 were found, so results are not yet shown.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14225, Immediate Expansion of American Timber Production, is signed; it sets 30 to 280 day deadlines for timber guidance, ESA consultation strategy, annual sale targets and NEPA categorical exclusions (published 2025-03-06).

USDA announces $23 million in grants to move hazardous fuels to processing facilities, giving priority to areas under Emergency Situation Determinations, and references the Secretary's directive to increase active forest management.

Secretary Rollins announces $200 million to implement the National Active Forest Management Strategy, with goals of 25 percent more national forest timber harvest and 4 billion board feet annually by fiscal year 2028.

Executive Order 14308, Empowering Commonsense Wildfire Prevention and Response, is signed; it directs consolidation of Interior and Agriculture wildland fire programs and review of rules that hinder prevention (published 2025-06-18).

USDA opens public comment on rescinding the 2001 Roadless Rule and announces an environmental impact statement; the rescission would cover about 45 million of nearly 60 million inventoried roadless acres.
The Forest Service publishes a proposed rule to streamline its project-level predecisional administrative review (objection) process.
The Forest Service consolidates national fire and aviation authorities under a single Deputy Chief for Fire and Aviation Management.

The Forest Service publishes a proposed rule to rescind the 2001 Roadless Rule (91 FR 53827, 36 CFR part 294), with comments due 2026-09-21; the same day Interior announces two NEPA categorical exclusions for BLM timber salvage and thinning projects.

Interior publishes two notices establishing BLM categorical exclusions for timber salvage harvest (91 FR 54739) and forest and woodland density management up to 5,000 acres (91 FR 54744), effective the same day; they apply to BLM-managed land, not national forests.

The Forest Service publishes a final rule revising its project-level predecisional objection process (91 FR 64760, 36 CFR part 218), shortening comment, objection and response periods, moving public notice to USDA websites and electronic notification, and aligning the process with USDA NEPA procedures; effective 2026-11-12.

uncertainties: The Forest Service's emergency situation determinations were referenced in a USDA release but the acreage and any litigation were not verified. Timber sale and harvest volumes since 2025 were not found, and the Fix Our Forests Act or other forest legislation was not checked. The Mandate recommendation to embrace Executive Order 13855 was not matched to an explicit reinstatement; the match is based on the content of Executive Orders 14225 and 14308. The Roadless Rule rescission is a proposal, not final. The 2026 timber categorical exclusions are Interior notices for BLM land (chapter 16 territory) that cite NEPA rather than Executive Order 14225; no Forest Service timber categorical exclusion rule was found in the Federal Register. The objection rule does not cite Executive Order 14225, so its link to the timber order is by content only.
